name: Masala Oats Upma
description: Savoury oats with colourful vegetables, curry leaves and lemon for a fast, fibre-rich breakfast.
ingredients: 1/2 cup diced carrot, beans and peas
Mustard seeds, cumin and curry leaves
steps: Dry-toast the oats for 3 minutes, then transfer them to a plate.
Heat oil and crackle mustard seeds, cumin and curry leaves; soften the onion.
Add the vegetables and tomato with a splash of water, cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in oats and 3/4 cup hot water, cook until fluffy, then finish with lemon and coriander.

name: Ragi Paneer Dosa
description: A crisp finger-millet dosa filled with spiced paneer and peppers for a satisfying protein-forward morning.
steps: Whisk ragi flour, rice flour, salt and water into a thin, lump-free batter.
Sear paneer, onion and capsicum with half the oil and spices until lightly charred.
Spread the batter thinly on a hot pan, drizzle with the remaining oil and cook until crisp.
Add the paneer filling, fold the dosa and serve with coriander and lemon.

name: Chicken Keema Poha
description: Fluffy turmeric poha folded with lean chicken keema and peas for an easy high-protein breakfast.
steps: Rinse poha briefly in a sieve and leave it to soften for 5 minutes.
Heat oil, saute onion and ginger, then add chicken mince, cumin, turmeric and salt.
Cook until the chicken is no longer pink, add peas and cook for another 3 minutes.
Fold in poha gently, warm through and finish with lemon and coriander.

name: Apple Cinnamon Overnight Oats
description: Creamy make-ahead oats layered with apple, yogurt and chia for a calm, practical start.
steps: Mix oats, yogurt, milk, chia, cinnamon and salt in a jar.
Fold in half the diced apple and add honey only if needed.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Stir, loosen with a splash of milk if needed and top with the remaining apple.

name: Sweet Potato Chickpea Hash
description: Crisp sweet potato, chickpeas and spinach with warm spices and lime.
steps: Microwave or steam the sweet-potato cubes for 4 minutes to begin softening them.
Heat oil in a wide pan and saute onion and capsicum until lightly browned.
Add sweet potato, chickpeas and spices; cook for 8 minutes, turning until crisp at the edges.
Fold in spinach until wilted and finish with lime and coriander.

name: Lemon Herb Chickpea Couscous
description: A bright chickpea and couscous bowl with crunchy vegetables, mint and lemon.
steps: Pour boiling water over the couscous, cover for 8 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil, pepper and salt into a dressing.
Combine couscous, chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, onion and herbs.
Toss with the dressing and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Palak Paneer Brown Rice
description: Spinach-rich paneer curry paired with brown basmati rice for a complete vegetarian lunch.
ingredients: Ginger, garlic, cumin and garam masala
steps: Blanch spinach for 2 minutes, cool it and blend until smooth.
Heat oil and cook onion, ginger and garlic; add tomato and spices until jammy.
Stir in spinach puree and paneer, then simmer gently for 6 minutes.
Serve with warm brown rice and a squeeze of lemon.

name: South Indian Sambar Rice
description: Comforting rice and lentils simmered with vegetables, tamarind and a fragrant curry-leaf tempering.
ingredients: 1 cup pumpkin, carrot and drumstick vegetable
steps: Simmer the vegetables and tomato with sambar powder, salt and enough water until tender.
Stir in cooked dal and tamarind, then simmer for 8 minutes.
Fold in the cooked rice and add hot water until softly spoonable.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil, pour over the rice and rest for 5 minutes.

name: Grilled Chicken Millet Salad
description: Herb-grilled chicken, millet and crisp vegetables in a fresh lemon dressing.
steps: Coat chicken with garlic, herbs, half the oil, lemon, pepper and salt.
Grill or pan-sear for 6-7 minutes per side, rest briefly and slice.
Combine millet, leaves, cucumber, tomatoes and roasted capsicum.
Dress with the remaining oil and lemon, then place the sliced chicken on top.

name: Egg Curry Quinoa Bowl
description: Tomato-onion egg curry with fluffy quinoa and cumin green beans.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel and halve them.
Heat half the oil and cook onion, ginger, tomato and spices into a thick masala.
Add a splash of water and the eggs, then simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Saute beans with cumin in the remaining oil and serve with quinoa and curry.

name: Sesame Tofu Noodle Bowl
description: Crisp tofu, whole-wheat noodles and crunchy vegetables in a gingery sesame sauce.
ingredients: 1 tsp sesame seeds and spring onion
steps: Cook the noodles until just tender, drain and reserve a little cooking water.
Sear tofu in a hot non-stick pan until golden on several sides.
Stir-fry the vegetables, ginger and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add noodles, tofu, soy sauce, sesame oil and a splash of cooking water; toss and garnish.

name: Mediterranean Lentil Feta Bowl
description: Herby lentils, crunchy vegetables, olives and feta in a lemony lunch bowl.
ingredients: 1 tsp olive oil, lemon, pepper and salt
steps: Drain and cool the cooked lentils completely.
Whisk olive oil, lemon, pepper and a small pinch of salt.
Combine lentils, cucumber, tomatoes, capsicum, olives and herbs.
Fold in feta gently, toss with the dressing and serve.

name: Mushroom Pea Masala with Roti
description: Mushrooms and peas in a rich tomato masala with soft whole-wheat rotis.
steps: Sear mushrooms in a dry hot pan until their moisture evaporates; set aside.
Heat oil and cook onion, ginger and garlic, then add tomato and spices.
Stir in peas, mushrooms and a splash of water; cover and simmer for 7 minutes.
Finish with coriander and serve with warm rotis.

name: Paneer Tikka Lettuce Wraps
description: Smoky paneer and peppers tucked into crisp lettuce cups with mint chutney.
steps: Coat paneer, capsicum and onion with yogurt, tandoori masala, ginger and salt.
Sear in oil on a hot pan until the vegetables soften and paneer chars at the edges.
Wash and dry the lettuce leaves thoroughly so they stay crisp.
Divide the tikka among the leaves and finish with mint chutney and lemon.

name: Ginger Lime Chicken Stir-Fry
description: Lean chicken and crisp vegetables in a bright ginger-lime glaze with brown rice.
steps: Mix soy sauce, lime juice, grated ginger, garlic and two tablespoons of water.
Stir-fry chicken in half the oil until browned and cooked through; remove briefly.
Add the remaining oil and vegetables, cooking over high heat for 4 minutes.
Return chicken, add the sauce and toss until glossy; serve with brown rice.

name: Baked Mustard Fish with Rice
description: Herbed mustard fish with lemon rice and charred green beans.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and line a small tray.
Coat fish with mustard, half the oil, garlic, parsley, lemon zest, pepper and salt.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until opaque and easily flaked; saute the beans meanwhile.
Fold lemon juice and turmeric through the warm rice and serve with fish and beans.

name: Red Lentil Vegetable Khichdi
description: A gentle one-pot khichdi with red lentils, rice and plenty of vegetables.
ingredients: 1 cup carrot, peas, spinach and tomato
steps: Heat oil in a saucepan and toast cumin, ginger and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add lentils, rice, vegetables, water and salt, then bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 22-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and creamy.
Adjust with hot water if needed and finish with pepper, coriander and lemon.

name: Quinoa-Stuffed Capsicum
description: Roasted peppers filled with quinoa, black beans, corn and a light feta topping.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and roast the empty capsicum halves for 10 minutes.
Mix quinoa, beans, corn, tomato, spices, coriander, lime and salt.
Pack the filling into the pepper halves and scatter feta over the top.
Bake for 15 minutes until the peppers are tender and the filling is hot.

name: Roasted Makhana Trail Cup
description: Crisp spiced fox nuts, chickpeas and pumpkin seeds for an easy savoury snack.
steps: Heat a wide pan and dry-roast makhana for 5 minutes until crisp.
Add oil and chickpeas, then cook for another 4 minutes.
Add pumpkin seeds, paprika, cumin, pepper and salt; toss for 1 minute.
Cool completely before eating or packing into an airtight container.

name: Mango Cardamom Lassi Bowl
description: Thick mango yogurt with cardamom, chia and fresh fruit in a spoonable snack bowl.
steps: Blend yogurt, half the mango, cardamom, salt and water until thick and smooth.
Taste and add honey only if the mango is not sweet enough.
Pour into a bowl and rest for 3 minutes after sprinkling on chia.
Top with the remaining mango and mint, then serve cold.

name: Hummus Cucumber Crunch
description: Creamy hummus with crisp cucumber, carrot and tomatoes for a no-cook snack plate.
steps: Blend chickpeas, tahini, olive oil, lemon, garlic, cumin and salt.
Add cold water one tablespoon at a time until the hummus is creamy.
Wash and cut the cucumber, carrot and tomatoes into easy dipping pieces.
Swirl hummus onto a plate, dust with paprika and arrange the vegetables alongside.

name: Chocolate Peanut Protein Bites
description: Chewy cocoa, oat and peanut bites for a compact pre- or post-workout snack.
steps: Pulse oats and dates in a small processor until crumbly.
Add peanut butter, sattu, cocoa, chia, cinnamon and salt.
Pulse again, adding a teaspoon of water only if the mixture will not hold.
Roll into six bites and chill for 20 minutes before eating.

name: Cottage Cheese Chaat
description: Fresh paneer, crunchy vegetables and pomegranate tossed with lemon and roasted cumin.
steps: Pat the paneer dry and cut it into small bite-sized cubes.
Combine cucumber, tomato, onion, pomegranate and herbs.
Add paneer, lemon, roasted cumin, chaat masala and a small pinch of salt.
Toss gently and eat immediately so the vegetables stay crisp.

name: Egg Cucumber Protein Box
description: Boiled eggs, crunchy vegetables and roasted chickpeas packed into a balanced snack box.
steps: Boil eggs for 9 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel.
Halve the eggs and season with pepper, paprika and a little salt.
Wash and slice the cucumber and tomatoes.
Arrange eggs, vegetables and roasted chickpeas in a divided container with lemon.

name: Spiced Corn Edamame Cup
description: Sweet corn and edamame tossed with peppers, coriander, chilli and lime.
steps: Boil or steam edamame and corn for 4 minutes, then drain well.
Warm oil in a pan and toss the corn, edamame and capsicum for 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and add lime, chilli, cumin, salt and pepper.
Fold in coriander and serve warm or chilled.

name: Date Sattu Energy Balls
description: Naturally sweet date and roasted-chickpea bites rolled in coconut for portable energy.
steps: Pulse the dates in a small processor until they form a sticky paste.
Add sattu, half the coconut, chia, cardamom, salt and optional cocoa.
Pulse until combined, adding only enough water for the mixture to hold.
Roll into six balls, coat with the remaining coconut and chill for 20 minutes.
